name: melfina
description: Melfina tool surface over HTTP — the MCP-first fallback for runtimes without MCP support.
precedence: Prefer the Melfina MCP server when available. Do not call both MCP and HTTP for the same operation.

auth.bearer: Authorization: Bearer $MELFINA_API_KEY — melf_… (dedicated), melfs_… (scoped), or melfg_… (fleet)
auth.basic: https://<agent name>:$MELFINA_API_KEY@host/api/tools/{tool} — Basic username pins the persona on fleet keys
auth.persona: fleet keys name the agent per call via the `name` argument, an X-Melfina-Agent-Key header, or the ?agent_key=<name> query param (names only)
auth.scopes: melfs_… keys carry a scope allowlist per tool; the `all:read` preset covers every `*:read` scope and `all:write` covers every scope
auth.credentials: injected by the target runtime ($MELFINA_API_KEY); never stored in generated files

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List every path in your private file tree.

name.description: Your agent name — your persona on this install. Required when the connection authenticates with the shared fleet key; on a dedicated key it must match that key's agent.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a file from your private file tree. Text comes back verbatim; images come back as MCP image content; other binaries need `format=base64` or a raw GET /api/files/{path}.

path.description: Path of the file to read, e.g. "notes/todo.txt".

format.description: Pass "base64" to read a non-image binary file — the result is a JSON payload with path, mime, and content_base64.

name.description: Your agent name — your persona on this install. Required when the connection authenticates with the shared fleet key; on a dedicated key it must match that key's agent.

tools.name: read_file_binary
tools.description: Read a binary file from your private file tree. Images come back as MCP image content (viewable natively); other binaries return a JSON payload with path, mime, and content_base64. For large downloads prefer `GET /api/files/{path}` — raw bytes, no base64. Text files belong on `read_file`.

path.description: Path of the binary file to read, e.g. "img/logo.png".

name.description: Your agent name — your persona on this install. Required when the connection authenticates with the shared fleet key; on a dedicated key it must match that key's agent.

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Write a file to your private file tree (overwrites existing content). Pass `content` for text; pass `content_base64` (+ optional `mime`) for binary — UTF-8 text stays a text file either way. For large binaries prefer PUT /api/files/{path}, which takes raw bytes without base64.

path.description: Path of the file to write, e.g. "notes/todo.txt".

content.description: Full text content to store (replaces existing). Required unless content_base64 is passed.

content_base64.description: Binary content, base64-encoded (replaces existing). Alternative to content for non-text files; bytes over ~1 MB belong on PUT /api/files/{path} instead.

mime.description: Declared content type for content_base64, e.g. "image/png". The stored mime always comes from sniffing the actual bytes.

name.description: Your agent name — your persona on this install. Required when the connection authenticates with the shared fleet key; on a dedicated key it must match that key's agent.

tools.name: write_file_binary
tools.description: Write a binary file (image, PDF, any non-text bytes) to your private file tree. Send the raw bytes in `content_base64` (base64-encoded); the stored mime is always sniffed from the actual bytes, so a wrong `mime` claim cannot stick. UTF-8 text written this way still lands as a normal text file. For payloads over ~1 MB prefer `PUT /api/files/{path}` — raw bytes, no base64 overhead.

path.description: Path of the file to write, e.g. "img/logo.png".

content_base64.description: Raw file bytes, base64-encoded (replaces existing). Bytes over ~1 MB belong on PUT /api/files/{path} instead.

mime.description: Declared content type, e.g. "image/png". The stored mime always comes from sniffing the actual bytes.

tools.name: knowledge_lookup
tools.description: Look up a named internal thing — a project, service, codename, decision, convention, runbook, person, event, or concept — in the shared knowledge base. Returns the wiki body plus a typed 1-hop neighborhood (predicate, peer, confidence). Names, aliases, persona names, and this agent's contextual titles resolve to the same canonical entity id. Internal nouns first, internet second: always try this before any external/web search when an unfamiliar proper noun appears. On a miss it says so plainly and suggests external lookup. Ambiguous names are not a miss — they return code ambiguous_reference and do not suggest the internet.

query.description: Canonical name, alias, persona name, this agent's contextual title, or the reserved word operator. Lookup returns the canonical entity; it does not change how you address anyone.

entry_id.description: Stable entity id. When supplied with query, both must name the same canonical entity.

ref.description: Structured installation role. Prefer ref=operator over relying on a person named Operator.

history.description: Also return wiki version history and recent graph observations.

hops.description: Neighborhood depth. 1 (default) is the typed 1-hop links payload; 2 also returns a bounded walk.

min_confidence.description: Hide links below this milli-confidence (0–1000). Default 0 so weak links stay visible.

name.description: Your agent name — your persona on this install. Required when the connection authenticates with the shared fleet key; on a dedicated key it must match that key's agent.

tools.name: knowledge_search
tools.description: Fuzzy-search the internal knowledge base when knowledge_lookup misses or you need broader context — matches canonical names, aliases, summaries, entry state, and this agent's contextual titles. Still internal-first: only escalate to external/web search when this returns nothing useful. An exact title match for this agent ranks the canonical person ahead of body-text hits. Other agents' titles are not searched.

query.description: Free-text search across names, aliases, this agent's contextual titles, summaries, and entry state.

name.description: Your agent name — your persona on this install. Required when the connection authenticates with the shared fleet key; on a dedicated key it must match that key's agent.

tools.name: knowledge_upsert
tools.description: Create or update a canonical knowledge entry — a project, service, decision, convention, runbook, person, or concept the install should know by name. `entry` is a target reference (canonical name, alias, persona name, or this agent's contextual title), not a rename: updating through an alias keeps the canonical name. Every write records a versioned snapshot with you as author. Pass expected_version to fail instead of clobbering a change someone else just made. Pass entry_id to pin the target; id and entry must agree.

entry.description: Target reference — canonical name, alias, persona name, or this agent's contextual title. Not a rename; the canonical name stays. (`name` stays reserved for your persona.)

entry_id.description: Stable entity id. When supplied with entry, both must name the same canonical entity.

aliases.description: Other global names this entry answers to (ordinary aliases). Does not add or remove scoped agent titles or persona/handle identifiers.

summary.description: One-line "what is this" — shown in search results.

state.description: Current state and important constraints — the durable facts.

source.description: Provenance — where this knowledge came from (doc, ticket, chat).

verified.description: Mark the entry as freshly verified — bumps verified_at.

expected_version.description: Optimistic-lock guard: only write if the entry is still at this version.

name.description: Your agent name — your persona on this install. Required when the connection authenticates with the shared fleet key; on a dedicated key it must match that key's agent.

tools.name: knowledge_connect
tools.description: Assert or retract a typed link between two internal knowledge entities, and attach the event data that justifies it. Use this to connect the dots — runs_on, depends_on, involves, owned_by — rather than stuffing names into knowledge_upsert related. Confidence rises when other agents independently assert the same link; the owner can lock a link permanent from the console. Missing endpoints are not created unless create_missing is true.

from.description: Canonical name, alias, persona name, or this agent's contextual title of the source entity.

to.description: Canonical name, alias, persona name, or this agent's contextual title of the target entity.

from_id.description: Stable source entity id. When supplied with from, both must name the same canonical entity.

to_id.description: Stable target entity id. When supplied with to, both must name the same canonical entity.

predicate.description: Typed meaning of the link. Inverse names (hosts, owns, …) are stored as the canonical opposite with ends swapped.

op.description: assert (default) strengthens the link; retract records a disagreement. Permanent links reject agent retracts.

data.description: Structured event payload for this assertion (version, host, ticket id, …).

source.description: Provenance — doc, ticket, chat, deploy log.

occurred_at.description: When the real-world event happened (ISO-8601). Distinct from when you recorded it.

event.description: If set, also upsert a named event entity and involve both ends.

create_missing.description: Create stub concept entities for unknown names. Default false so typos do not spawn nodes.

name.description: Your agent name — your persona on this install. Required when the connection authenticates with the shared fleet key; on a dedicated key it must match that key's agent.

tools.name: knowledge_add_alias
tools.description: Add another name for an existing knowledge entity. An alias is the same entity — a project, a place, or a person — not a separate presentation. Lookup of the alias returns that entity.

entry.description: Target entity: canonical name, alias, or this agent's contextual title.

entry_id.description: Stable entity id. When supplied with entry, both must name the same entity.

alias.description: Another name for this same entity.

name.description: Your agent name — your persona on this install. Required when the connection authenticates with the shared fleet key; on a dedicated key it must match that key's agent.

tools.name: knowledge_link_persona
tools.description: Link two person entries as the same living being with different presentations. Lookup keeps each entry's own name and reports that they are equal. This does not rename either person.

person_id.description: Stable id for person. When supplied, it must agree with person.

persona.description: The other person entry — a different presentation of the same being.

persona_id.description: Stable id for persona. When supplied, it must agree with persona.

name.description: Your agent name — your persona on this install. Required when the connection authenticates with the shared fleet key; on a dedicated key it must match that key's agent.
